answer: One workable design: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because onyx only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, timber is enforced in the ledger: Independence is measured by who attests to whom, which is expensive to fake at scale. Any bridge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
